clue.text: Extended picnic?

definitions.meaning: stretched or laid out at full length
a cryptic sense: a meal laid on a cloth outdoors is a spread put out of doors

explanation.surface: A long, leisurely meal on the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extended is stretched across a space; a picnic is food set out as a spread, outside.

clue.text: Not required to be forgiving

definitions.meaning: to let someone off, show mercy

explanation.surface: Someone told that mercy is unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra items are not needed; and to let off a captive is a merciful act of forgiveness.

clue.text: Poster I designed brings sharp response

indicators.note: the letters of the words are arranged anew, as a designer lays out a fresh pattern

explanation.surface: A graphic artist's poster provokes a cutting reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, witty retort, originally a fencer's counter-thrust after parrying.

clue.text: Oriental perhaps like a Scotsman?

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Asking whether an Easterner resembles a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the East of the world is, for example, from that continent; the 'perhaps' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: The edition you pick up in the street?

definitions.meaning: a collected volume of several works in one

definitions.text: you pick up in the street?
definitions.meaning: a public road vehicle that collects passengers, an old word for a bus

explanation.surface: A newspaper you grab from a street vendor.
explanation.definitionFit: A collected volume of several works, or a run of episodes shown together, carries the same name as an old word for a bus.

clue.text: One may have designs on your body

definitions.text: One may have designs on your body

parts.words: One may have designs on your body
parts.note: having designs on someone suggests a seducer, but here it is literal: an artist inking pictures on skin

explanation.surface: A warning about someone with predatory intentions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have designs on' is the idiom for scheming to get someone; read literally, it is ink on skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who inks permanent pictures into skin literally puts designs on a body.

clue.text: Total pressure in reservoir

parts.note: a sum is a total
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: The combined pressure in a water reservoir.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit or well where liquid such as engine oil collects is a kind of reservoir.

clue.text: On a fine day, time for reading here in the garden?

definitions.text: On a fine day, time for reading here in the garden?

parts.words: On a fine day, time for reading here in the garden?
parts.note: suggests a bench for reading a book in sunshine, but the thing read is the time, shown by a shadow

explanation.surface: An invitation to read outdoors when the weather is good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time for reading' seems to mean leisure for a book; it is the time that gets read, and only in sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden instrument whose shadow-casting pointer shows the hour, usable only when the sun is out.

clue.text: '80s child has shed pounds for a very long time

indicators.note: shedding means dropping something, so a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: a millennial is someone born in the 1980s or 1990s
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A young adult has lost weight over a long stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousands of years together make an extremely long period.

clue.text: Returning computer nuisance, it's said, in military operations

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer

indicators.note: what is spoken is matched by sound, not by spelling

parts.note: a pain is a nuisance

explanation.surface: A recurring computer annoyance during army operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns MAC into CAM; 'it's said' means PAIN is heard as the ending PAIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised series of battles or manoeuvres in a war is a campaign.

clue.text: Feel excited anticipation in time at fireside

parts.note: an ingle is a fireplace or hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Sitting by the fire, thrilled at what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrill with a prickling, nervous excitement before something happens.

clue.text: So near sports ground

indicators.note: to sport is to play or frolic, so the letters play around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lives close to a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports ground' reads as one phrase; 'sports' is the anagram signal and 'ground' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds for something are its basis or justification, a cause or motive.

clue.text: Newly-weds receiving order for sedatives

indicators.note: taking in something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: brides are women just married
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A just-married couple are given a prescription for calming pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium salts once used as calming drugs; the word also means a trite, soothing remark.

clue.text: In addition, no worse

explanation.surface: A comment that something is also no worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'also', and 'you might as well' says one course is equally good.

clue.text: Post delivered by householder?

parts.note: a creature carrying its house on its back is the householder, and slow letters are named after it

explanation.surface: Letters dropped off by the person living at the address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'householder' seems to mean a resident; it is a creature that carries its shell-house.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary letters sent by the postal service, called slow compared with email.

clue.text: Girl closes hackneyed religious ceremony

indicators.note: the girl closes round, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: lass is a girl
trite means hackneyed, overused

explanation.surface: A girl wraps up a stale church ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacraments given by a priest to a person who is dying form a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Son ready for heavy drinking

parts.note: willing means ready, prepared to do something

explanation.surface: A son eager to go on a binge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulping down drink greedily in large quantities.

clue.text: Sober lad goes wild — he can't take defeat

indicators.note: running riot, so the letters lose their order and rearrange

explanation.surface: A teetotal youth runs amok because he cannot accept losing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sulks or rages after a loss is a poor sport.

clue.text: Bird's circuit over part of mansion

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
a wing is a section of a large house

explanation.surface: A bird circling above one side of a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit, a crested plover of farmland, is a bird.

clue.text: Unwillingly involves person I sacked

indicators.note: sacked as in a city plundered and wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone drags a dismissed employee into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone, often reluctantly, to take part is to rope them into it.

clue.text: Scottish design nationalist renegade rejected

indicators.note: thrown back, so the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: Nat is short for a nationalist, as in the Scottish Nationalists
a rat is a turncoat or deserter

explanation.surface: A Scottish nationalist who switched sides is cast out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns NATRAT round, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The checked woollen cloth of the Highlands, each pattern linked to a clan.

clue.text: Look embarrassed to lose energy, a warning sign

parts.note: to go red is to look embarrassed
to flag is to tire or weaken

explanation.surface: Blushing and wilting are signs of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarlet banner signals danger, so the phrase means any warning of a problem.

clue.text: Applaud role reversal? Nonsense

parts.note: to clap is to applaud

indicators.note: the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Cheering an actor who swaps roles is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty, pretentious talk is rubbish or drivel.

clue.text: Put on an extra court for heroin user, say

parts.note: to put on an extra one is to add one, ADD plus I (one)

explanation.surface: Building another court for the benefit of a drug user.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on an extra' is read as 'add one': ADD plus I, the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependent on a drug; a heroin user is one example, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Cutting a crossing

parts.note: Xing is the road-sign abbreviation for a crossing, as in Ped Xing

explanation.surface: A place where a road is cut through.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping with a hatchet; also slashing jobs or budgets.

clue.text: At sea once, a small boat

indicators.note: confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being afloat in a little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, narrow paddled craft is a small boat.

clue.text: Miserable meeting first vicious man

parts.note: sad means miserable
1st, written with the digit as the letter I, is first

explanation.surface: An unhappy first encounter with a cruel man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes pleasure in inflicting pain is a cruel, vicious person.

clue.text: Pass over country road in Arctic transport

parts.note: to skip is to pass over, omit
a lane is a narrow country road

explanation.surface: Flying over a rural road in polar regions.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft fitted with runners to land on snow is used to get around the frozen north.

clue.text: Supposedly black comedian malign at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so its middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: A comedian whose identity is maligned at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The character is Sacha Baron Cohen's spoof wannabe street rapper from west London, who claims his treatment is 'because I is black'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fictional comic persona played by a white actor who pretends to be black.

clue.text: A guy's gone off to find a religious assembly

indicators.note: gone off as in spoiled or wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone has left to look for a church gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish congregation, or the building where it meets for worship.
